products.name: ShareGate Migrate
products.role: Copies sites, OneDrive, teams and mailboxes between tenants, as a tool run by an administrator.
before: Add the application to the EWS allow list of the source and of the target.
Create the target resource mailboxes first: the copy does not create them.
during: Run a pre-copy, then a final copy after the sources are frozen.
after: Reconcile the volumes, then redo by hand what the tool does not copy, such as calendar folder permissions.

license.text: Copy mailboxes and PowerShell need the Pro or Enterprise plan: neither is in Essentials.

limits.text: A single mailbox moves at 1.5 GB per hour at most. The publisher advises against one copy action of more than 800,000 items.
Copy mailboxes goes through EWS: the application must be on the allow list of both tenants until the retirement.
Shared channels are not supported.
The 50 most recent conversations go to the Posts tab. A PowerShell parameter copies up to 500 messages there. All the conversations stay in an HTML archive page, in a new Message history tab.
Resource mailboxes: only events organized by the resource are copied, and the target mailbox must already exist.
Private chats: in-chat file attachment links do not move, and meeting chats arrive as group chats.

products.name: Quest On Demand Migration
products.role: Hosted service for migrations between tenants.
before: Ask the publisher whether mail tasks still use EWS.
during: Move OneDrive before private chats: chat attachments point to it.

license.text: Licensed per source account handled, consumed when the task starts. Confirm which plan includes chats.

limits.text: Mail tasks still used EWS at the last publication read. Confirm the move to Graph.
Move OneDrive first: chat attachments are linked to it.

products.name: BitTitan MigrationWiz
products.role: Hosted service that moves mail and data between tenants, by project.
before: Check whether an old project left an application or a consent in a tenant.

license.text: The Tenant Migration Bundle includes the User Migration Bundle, and either Teams Migration or Shared Documents of 100 GB.

limits.text: A Graph mailbox project is available. EWS stays in use for what Graph does not cover yet: some archives, public folders and group mailboxes.
Shared channels are not migrated.
Private chats are part of the User Migration Bundle.

products.name: Microsoft cross-tenant migration
products.role: Native move of mailboxes, OneDrive, chats and meetings, inside Microsoft 365. SharePoint is a separate service.

license.text: Cross Tenant User Data Migration: a one-time license per user, on the source or the target user object. It also covers OneDrive.

rights.text: The target account must exist as a mail user, prepared with the attributes of the source mailbox.

dataLocation.text: The data never leaves the Microsoft 365 cloud.

limits.text: The target must be a mail user with no mailbox: it cannot merge into an existing account.
A OneDrive that already exists at the target makes the move fail.
OneDrive moves once: no incremental or delta pass.
The orchestrator covers four workloads: mailboxes, OneDrive, Teams chats and Teams meetings. Teams and channels are not among them.
Mailboxes on any hold are not migrated: the move is blocked.
SharePoint needs its own license, Cross-Tenant Shared Data Migration, offered per 100 GB of data moved and only to Enterprise Agreement customers.

products.name: TenantConverge assessment
products.role: Reads the tenants, then computes the findings, the score and the plan that this report shows.
before: Have the read-only application approved, when access is by application.
after: Remove the read-only application with Remove-TcAccess.

products.name: TenantConverge remediations
products.role: Separate scripts that act on a decisions file, with a preview by default.
before: Read each script, and try it on a test tenant.

products.name: AvePoint Cloud Backup
products.role: Backup of Microsoft 365, including Teams chat as its own service.
before: Check the last backup and restore a test item.
If chats stay readable through the backup, test that restore.
after: Test access to the data after a tenant closes.

limits.text: Teams chat does not support a retention policy: its backups stay until the subscription ends.
Exporting data before it is deleted is a paid service.

products.name: Datto SaaS Protection
products.role: Backup of OneDrive, Exchange, SharePoint and Teams.
before: Confirm how new accounts join the backup.
after: Try a restore on a migrated account.

limits.text: 1:1 Teams chats are not backed up.
Public folders and Planner are not covered.

products.name: Check Point Harmony Email & Collaboration
products.role: Mail security that can run inline, through connectors and mail flow rules.
before: Bring the domains and accounts that move into the protected scope.
during: Test inbound and outbound flow for each domain that moves.
after: Remove the connector and rules of a source when it closes.

limits.text: Inline protection needs the option that retains internal Exchange headers on the outbound connector. Keep it when reconfiguring.
In inline mode, its Protect rule goes first in the list of mail flow rules.

products.name: KnowBe4 and PhishER
products.role: Security awareness training, and handling of reported messages.
before: Validate the inbound connector for the domains that move.
after: Remove the integration of a source when it closes.

products.name: CrowdStrike Falcon
products.role: Endpoint protection, often deployed through Intune.
before: Include the agent in the device reset test.
after: Remove the old devices from the console.

products.name: Hornetsecurity 365 Total Protection
products.role: Mail security for Microsoft 365, in MX, API or hybrid mode.
before: Confirm that it is in use. If not, remove its applications and its SPF entry.

products.name: Leftovers of former mail filters
products.role: Disabled rules or connectors left by a mail filtering service that is gone.
before: Confirm that the service is gone, then remove what it left.

products.name: CodeTwo Email Signatures 365
products.role: Adds signatures to outgoing mail, at the server or in Outlook.
before: Recreate the signatures of the sources in the target, and test with an account of each group.
after: Remove the applications of a source when it closes.

limits.text: Rules move between tenants by export and import.
Separate signatures per domain need one rule per domain.

products.name: NinjaOne
products.role: Endpoint management and remote access. It can list the applications installed on devices.
before: Export the installed applications and validate them with their owners.
after: Check that the agent comes back on reset devices.

products.name: Windows Autopilot and Intune
products.role: Resets Windows devices and enrolls them in a tenant from their hardware identity.
before: Try the reset on a pilot device.
after: Remove the old profiles of the source.

limits.text: A device that leaves an organization should be deregistered from Autopilot: delete it from Intune first, then deregister it.

products.name: Cloudflare
products.role: DNS host with an API.
before: Get an API token limited to the zones that move.
during: Update MX, SPF, Autodiscover and DKIM.

products.name: GoDaddy
products.role: Domain registrar and DNS host.
before: Get access to the zone.

products.name: Amazon Route 53
products.role: DNS service of Amazon Web Services.
before: Get access to the hosted zone.

products.name: Microsoft Calling Plans
products.role: Microsoft as the telephony carrier for Teams.
before: Choose the target model, then order the porting.
after: Recreate auto attendants, call queues and schedules in the target.

products.name: Teams Direct Routing
products.role: Connects Teams to a carrier through a certified session border controller.
before: Identify the provider and its porting terms.

products.name: Operator Connect
products.role: Teams telephony run by a partner operator.

products.name: Line-of-business applications
products.role: Applications that sign in through Entra ID or send mail for the business.
before: List them from the enterprise applications of each source.
during: Give access to the migrated accounts that need it.

products.name: Security monitoring applications
products.role: Applications of a monitoring provider that read the logs of a tenant.
before: Confirm the scope once a source closes.

products.name: Bulk mail platforms
products.role: Bulk mail platforms that domains allow through SPF.
before: Keep these entries when merging SPF, if they are still in use.

sharegate.note: Covered, with the EWS allow list, at 1.5 GB per hour per mailbox.

quest.note: Covered. Confirm whether mail tasks still use EWS.

bittitan.note: Covered, by a Graph or an EWS project.

microsoft-xt.note: Covered if the target account has no mailbox yet.

sharegate.note: The destination exists by design. Try how the items are filed.

microsoft-xt.note: Not possible: neither a mailbox nor a OneDrive may exist at the target.
One move, with no incremental pass.

bittitan.note: Through Shared Documents, 100 GB per license.

microsoft-xt.note: One move, for Enterprise Agreement customers.

sharegate.note: Covered, with the history in an HTML archive tab.

microsoft-xt.note: Teams and channels are not a workload of the orchestrator.

sharegate.note: By PowerShell. In-chat attachment links do not move.

microsoft-xt.note: Not a workload of the orchestrator.

exposure.label: Largest mailbox
exposure.some: At 1.5 GB per hour, a pre-copy of this mailbox takes about {hours} hours. Start it several days before the cutover.

exposure.label: Sites of 100 GB or more
exposure.some: They hold {volume} GB: they shape the copy plan.

exposure.label: Likely duplicate accounts
exposure.some: The native Microsoft move refuses them: a mailbox or OneDrive already at the target makes it fail.

exposure.label: Bookings pages
exposure.some: Plan to recreate or retire them, and check that none keeps a domain in use.

exposure.label: Shared channels
exposure.some: ShareGate does not support them: recreate them by hand.

exposure.label: Planner plans
exposure.some: Validate the copy during the pilot.

exposure.label: Microsoft 365 groups
exposure.some: Check how the chosen tool copies group mailboxes: some still use EWS for them.

exposure.label: Mailboxes with an archive
exposure.some: Plan the archive copy: some tools still use EWS for it.
exposure.none: No active archive: no archive copy to plan.

exposure.label: Mailboxes on hold
exposure.some: The native Microsoft move blocks a mailbox on any hold.
exposure.none: No hold: nothing blocks a native move on this ground.

exposure.label: Kiosk, F1 or F3 licenses
exposure.some: These licenses have no EWS rights, even with the allow list: give them another license for the copy.

milestones.title: Blocked by default
milestones.text: EWS is disabled in tenants that did not keep it enabled with an allow list. Admins can turn it back on for a time.

milestones.title: Final shutdown
milestones.text: EWS is permanently disabled, whatever the tenant settings.

dependencies.name: ShareGate
dependencies.text: Copy mailboxes goes through EWS. The publisher says it is working with Microsoft to stop needing it.

dependencies.name: Quest
dependencies.text: Mail tasks still used EWS at the last publication read. Confirm the move to Graph.

dependencies.name: BitTitan
dependencies.text: A Graph project is available. EWS stays in use for some archives, public folders and group mailboxes.

dependencies.name: Microsoft
dependencies.text: The native move goes through the mailbox move service of Exchange Online. Its page does not list EWS as a requirement.

cautions: Setting EwsAllowedAppIDs replaces the whole list each time: read it, complete it, then write it back.
This setting touches the whole tenant: get the agreement of its owner.
Kiosk, F1 and F3 licenses have no EWS rights, even with the list.
The assessment does not read EwsAllowedAppIDs: check it in each tenant.
